# EUDR guidance for coffee and cocoa operators

This guidance is addressed to operators and traders that import coffee (CN 0901) and cocoa (CN 1801, 1803, 1804, 1805, 1806) into the Union. It complements the general Guidance Document on Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 and does not cover other relevant commodities such as wood, rubber, soya, oil palm or cattle products.

Coffee and cocoa importers shall submit a due diligence statement in the EUDR Information System before customs release of each consignment. Where beans are sourced from smallholder cooperatives, importers shall obtain the geolocation of every farm, either as a point for farms below four hectares or as a polygon for larger plots.

Importers of roasted coffee or chocolate products shall reference the due diligence statements of their upstream suppliers instead of collecting geolocation again, provided that those statements were submitted within the Union. Operators are reminded that the simplified due diligence for low-risk countries still requires the collection of the information set out in Article 9 of the Regulation.

# Consumer Rights Directive

The Consumer Rights Directive (2011/83/EU) gives consumers the same rights wherever they shop in the EU: clear pre-contractual information, a 14-day right of withdrawal for online and off-premises purchases, and a ban on hidden charges.
The Directive was amended in 2023 to require an online withdrawal function; Member States apply the new rules from 19 June 2026.

# Directive (EU) 2023/2673 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 November 2023

amending Directive 2011/83/EU as regards financial services contracts concluded at a distance and repealing Directive 2002/65/EC

## Article 1 — Amendments to Directive 2011/83/EU

(4) the following Article is inserted:

### Article 11a — Exercise of the right of withdrawal for contracts concluded by means of an online interface

1. In the case of contracts concluded by means of an online interface, the trader shall ensure that the consumer can also exercise the right of withdrawal by means of a withdrawal function. The withdrawal function shall be labelled with the words 'withdraw contract here' or a corresponding unambiguous formulation in an easily legible manner. The withdrawal function shall be continuously available during the withdrawal period. It shall be prominently displayed on the online interface and easily accessible to the consumer.

2. The withdrawal function shall allow the consumer to send an online withdrawal statement informing the trader of the consumer's decision to withdraw from the contract. That online withdrawal statement shall allow the consumer to provide or confirm easily the following information:

(a) the consumer's name;

(b) details identifying the contract from which the consumer wants to withdraw;

(c) details of the electronic means by which the confirmation of withdrawal is to be sent to the consumer.

3. Once the consumer has filled in the online withdrawal statement in accordance with paragraph 2, the trader shall enable the consumer to submit it by means of a confirmation function. That confirmation function shall be labelled in an easily legible manner only with the words 'confirm withdrawal' or a corresponding unambiguous formulation.

4. When the consumer submits the online withdrawal statement, the trader shall communicate to the consumer without undue delay an acknowledgement of receipt of the withdrawal on a durable medium, including its content and the date and time of submission.

5. The consumer shall be deemed to have exercised the right of withdrawal within the relevant withdrawal period if the consumer submitted the online withdrawal statement referred to in this Article before that period has expired.

## Article 2 — Transposition

1. Member States shall adopt and publish, by 19 December 2025, the measures necessary to comply with this Directive. They shall apply those measures from 19 June 2026.

# Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 31 May 2023

on the making available on the Union market and the export from the Union of certain commodities and products associated with deforestation and forest degradation and repealing Regulation (EU) No 995/2010

## Article 1 — Subject matter and scope

1. This Regulation lays down rules regarding the placing and making available on the Union market, as well as the export from the Union, of relevant products, as listed in Annex I, that contain, have been fed with or have been made using relevant commodities, namely cattle, cocoa, coffee, oil palm, rubber, soya and wood.

## Article 3 — Prohibition

Relevant commodities and relevant products shall not be placed or made available on the market or exported, unless all the following conditions are fulfilled: (a) they are deforestation-free; (b) they have been produced in accordance with the relevant legislation of the country of production; and (c) they are covered by a due diligence statement.

## Article 4 — Obligations of operators

1. Operators shall exercise due diligence in accordance with Article 8 prior to placing relevant products on the market or exporting them in order to demonstrate that the relevant products comply with Article 3.

2. Operators shall, prior to placing the relevant products on the market or exporting them, make available to the competent authorities via the information system referred to in Article 33 a due diligence statement confirming that due diligence was exercised and that no or only a negligible risk was found.

## Article 9 — Information requirements

1. Operators shall collect information, documents and data demonstrating that the relevant products comply with Article 3. For this purpose, the operator shall collect, organise and keep for 5 years the following information relating to each relevant product, accompanied by evidence:

(d) the geolocation of all plots of land where the relevant commodities that the relevant product contains, or has been made using, were produced, as well as the date or time range of production;

## Article 31 — Record keeping

Operators shall keep for at least 5 years from the date of the placing on the market or export of the relevant products all documentation related to due diligence, in particular the due diligence statement, and shall make it available to the competent authorities upon request.

## Article 38 — Entry into force and application

Articles 3 to 13 shall apply from 30 December 2025; for operators that by 31 December 2020 were established as micro-undertakings or small undertakings they shall apply from 30 June 2026.

# Regulation (EU) 2024/3234 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024

amending Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 as regards provisions relating to the date of application. Article 38 is amended so that Articles 3 to 13 apply from 30 December 2025, and from 30 June 2026 for operators or traders that by 31 December 2020 were established as micro-undertakings or small undertakings.

# Directive 2011/83/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 October 2011 on consumer rights

Consolidated text as last amended by Directive (EU) 2023/2673. The Directive harmonises the pre-contractual information and the 14-day right of withdrawal for distance and off-premises contracts across the Union.
Article 11a (withdrawal function) applies to contracts concluded from 19 June 2026.

# Implementation of the Deforestation Regulation

The Regulation on deforestation-free products (EU) 2023/1115 applies from 30 December 2025 for large and medium operators and from 30 June 2026 for micro and small enterprises.
This page collects the Guidance Document, the FAQ, the country benchmarking list and access to the EUDR Information System where due diligence statements are submitted.

# EU withdrawal function

From 19 June 2026, stores that sell to customers in the European Union need to offer a withdrawal function so customers can cancel a contract in two steps: fill in a withdrawal form, then confirm it.
You can enable the withdrawal function in your checkout settings; Shopify sends the customer an automatic confirmation email with the date and time of the withdrawal.

# US return and refund rules

If you sell to customers in the United States, then federal and state rules affect how you handle returns and refunds. The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule requires that you ship orders within the time stated in your ad or, if no time is stated, within 30 days.

When you can't ship on time, you must notify the customer and offer the option to cancel the order for a full refund. Refunds for cancelled orders must be issued within seven working days for card payments. The FTC does not require you to accept returns of delivered goods, but if you post a return policy you must honor it.

Some states, such as California and New York, require that you display your return and refund policy conspicuously at the point of sale. If no policy is displayed, customers in those states may return goods for a full refund within a statutory period. These rules apply only to sales to customers located in the United States; they do not cover the withdrawal rights of consumers in the European Union.

# Widerrufsbutton im Online-Handel

Ab dem 19. Juni 2026 müssen Online-Händler Verbraucherinnen und Verbrauchern eine Widerrufsfunktion („Widerrufsbutton") anbieten, mit der ein Fernabsatzvertrag in zwei Schritten widerrufen werden kann.
Die Regelung setzt die Richtlinie (EU) 2023/2673 um und ist in § 356a BGB geregelt.

# Entwaldungsfreie Lieferketten (EUDR)

Die EU-Verordnung über entwaldungsfreie Lieferketten gilt für Rind, Kakao, Kaffee, Ölpalme, Kautschuk, Soja und Holz sowie für daraus hergestellte Erzeugnisse wie Leder, Möbel und Papier.
Zuständige Behörde in Deutschland ist die Bundesanstalt für Landwirtschaft und Ernährung (BLE); die Pflichten gelten ab dem 30. Dezember 2025, für Kleinst- und Kleinunternehmen ab dem 30. Juni 2026.

# Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch (BGB) — § 356a Widerrufsrecht bei im elektronischen Geschäftsverkehr geschlossenen Verträgen

(1) Bei einem im elektronischen Geschäftsverkehr geschlossenen Verbrauchervertrag, der dem Verbraucher ein Widerrufsrecht nach § 312g Absatz 1 gewährt, hat der Unternehmer sicherzustellen, dass der Verbraucher das Widerrufsrecht auch durch eine Widerrufsfunktion ausüben kann. Die Widerrufsfunktion ist mit den Worten „Vertrag hier widerrufen" oder mit einer entsprechenden eindeutigen Formulierung in gut lesbarer Form zu kennzeichnen. Sie ist während der Widerrufsfrist durchgehend verfügbar zu halten sowie auf der Online-Benutzeroberfläche gut sichtbar und für den Verbraucher leicht zugänglich zu platzieren.

(2) Die Widerrufsfunktion muss es dem Verbraucher ermöglichen, eine Widerrufserklärung abzugeben, mit der er den Unternehmer über seinen Entschluss informiert, den Vertrag zu widerrufen. Die Widerrufserklärung muss es dem Verbraucher ermöglichen, die folgenden Angaben leicht zu machen oder zu bestätigen:

1. seinen Namen,
2. Angaben zur Identifizierung des Vertrags, den er widerrufen möchte,
3. Angaben zu dem elektronischen Kommunikationsmittel, über das ihm die Bestätigung des Widerrufs zu übermitteln ist.

(3) Nach dem Ausfüllen der Widerrufserklärung hat der Unternehmer dem Verbraucher zu ermöglichen, die Widerrufserklärung über eine Bestätigungsfunktion abzusenden. Die Bestätigungsfunktion ist in gut lesbarer Form ausschließlich mit den Worten „jetzt widerrufen" oder mit einer entsprechenden eindeutigen Formulierung zu kennzeichnen.

(4) Gibt der Verbraucher die Widerrufserklärung ab, hat der Unternehmer dem Verbraucher unverzüglich auf einem dauerhaften Datenträger den Eingang der Widerrufserklärung zu bestätigen, einschließlich ihres Inhalts sowie des Datums und der Uhrzeit ihres Eingangs.

(5) Der Verbraucher hat das Widerrufsrecht innerhalb der Widerrufsfrist ausgeübt, wenn er die Widerrufserklärung nach Absatz 2 vor Ablauf der Widerrufsfrist abgesendet hat.

Fußnote: § 356a gilt für Verträge, die ab dem 19. Juni 2026 geschlossen werden (Artikel 229 § 68 EGBGB).

# Widerrufsbutton: Was Online-Händler ab Juni 2026 beachten müssen

Online-Shops müssen ab dem 19. Juni 2026 eine gut sichtbare Widerrufsfunktion mit der Beschriftung „Vertrag hier widerrufen" anbieten, gefolgt von einer Bestätigungsseite mit „jetzt widerrufen".
Nach dem Widerruf ist dem Kunden unverzüglich eine Eingangsbestätigung auf einem dauerhaften Datenträger, etwa per E-Mail, zu übermitteln.

# EUDR: Fristen für Kleinst- und Kleinunternehmen

Die EU-Entwaldungsverordnung (Verordnung (EU) 2023/1115, EUDR) gilt für Unternehmen, die Rind, Kakao, Kaffee, Ölpalme, Kautschuk, Soja oder Holz sowie daraus hergestellte Erzeugnisse wie Möbel, Papier oder Lederwaren in der EU in Verkehr bringen oder ausführen. Nach der Verschiebung durch die Verordnung (EU) 2024/3234 gelten die Pflichten für Marktteilnehmer und Händler ab dem 30. Dezember 2025.

Kleinst- und Kleinunternehmen müssen die Pflichten erst ab dem 30. Juni 2026 erfüllen. Maßgeblich ist, ob das Unternehmen am 31. Dezember 2020 die Schwellenwerte der Richtlinie 2013/34/EU unterschritten hat: Ein Kleinstunternehmen überschreitet höchstens einen der Werte Bilanzsumme 350.000 Euro, Nettoumsatz 700.000 Euro oder zehn Beschäftigte im Jahresdurchschnitt; ein Kleinunternehmen höchstens einen der Werte 4 Millionen Euro Bilanzsumme, 8 Millionen Euro Umsatz oder 50 Beschäftigte.

Unternehmen müssen daher zunächst ihre Größenklasse anhand von Umsatz, Bilanzsumme und Beschäftigtenzahl bestimmen, bevor sie wissen, welche Frist für sie gilt. Händler, die keine KMU sind, müssen bereits ab dem 30. Dezember 2025 Sorgfaltserklärungen abgeben oder auf die Erklärungen ihrer Lieferanten verweisen. Die IHK empfiehlt, die Referenznummern der Sorgfaltserklärungen von Lieferanten frühzeitig anzufordern und aufzubewahren.

# The EU withdrawal button: what merchants need to know before 19 June 2026

The amended Consumer Rights Directive requires every online store selling to EU consumers to add a clearly labelled withdrawal button, followed by a confirmation step and a receipt on a durable medium.
This post walks through the two-step flow, the required labels and how to prepare your store before the deadline.

# EUDR compliance for ecommerce merchants

The EU Deforestation Regulation covers wood, leather (cattle), coffee, cocoa, rubber, soy and palm oil, and the products made from them, including furniture, paper and chocolate.
If you place these products on the EU market you need due diligence statements from your suppliers and the geolocation of the plots where the raw material was grown.
